citation.authors: Rappelt L, Held S, Wiedenmann T, Deutsch J-P, Hochstrate J, Wicker P, Donath L
citation.title: Restricted nasal-only breathing during self-selected low intensity training does not affect training intensity distribution

population.description: Nineteen physically healthy adults, 3 female, who had pursued an endurance sport for at least 2 years (3 or more sessions a week) and had no medical condition that would prevent the sessions (Methods 2.1). Age 26.5 ± 5.1 y, height 1.77 ± 0.08 m, body mass 77.3 ± 11.4 kg, VO2peak 53.4 ± 6.6 mL/kg/min (Methods 2.1). No BMI is printed, so bmi is null. Whole group; no split. The paper calls the group 'physically healthy' and screened no further, so status is healthy; they are endurance-trained (at least 2 years, 3 or more sessions a week), which is not a split of the group.

protocols.name: oronasal_bout
protocols.description: 60 min of self-selected low-intensity cycling, ordinary oro-nasal (unrestricted) breathing, about 80 rpm, no mouth tape or nasal dilators (Methods 2.3; Results 3.1). Activity level per 10-min interval from Table 2's measured oxygen uptake (Unrestricted row, 2.49, 2.59, 2.59, 2.57, 2.60, 2.61 l/min for T10 to T60): level = (VO2 x 1000 / 77.3 - 3.7) / 31.7 with the group's mean mass 77.3 kg (Methods 2.1), giving 0.8994, 0.9402, 0.9402, 0.9321, 0.9443, 0.9484 for minutes 0-10 up to 50-61 (ratio of means). Table 1 power / 186 would give 0.77 to 0.82, about 0.1 lower; the README's measured-VO2 rule takes precedence (gross efficiency 15.7-17.7%). The last segment runs to minute 61 so the T60 lactate sample falls with the input on, as bradley-2015 does. No food, fasting state or clock hour printed, only the same time of day per visit and no strenuous exercise in the prior 24 h: no meal, norm_center start, clock hour assumed (10.0); duration 61 min assumed.
